Waist-high and full-body cover distributed evenly across every lane inside the walls
Narrow transitions where the lanes meet, concentrating gunfights into contested ground
Balanced bases at opposite ends of the walled square, shielded from sniper lines
A flag stand at each team base, scored by carrying the enemy flag back to it

A flag stand per team, scored by carrying something to it or holding it against contest

notes: Preset Team Deathmatch kept with its shape lane-network; capture-zone added from the prompt's capture-the-flag mode.
barrier-perimeter taken from Sports via options.md — Shooter's own table and the universal six have no perimeter-wall row, and the hollow square wall is the only geometry the prompt states outright.

One map is asked to serve free-for-all, team deathmatch and capture the flag. The layout unions what those modes need (two mirrored bases plus a flag stand each) rather than committing to one mode; free-for-all in particular sits awkwardly with two mirrored bases and may want scattered spawns.
Scale assumed at the block band: the prompt says 'huge' without naming anything that lives inside, and an arcade shooter arena with cover and chokepoints reads at 100-500 studs.
End of run inferred from the genre and modes rather than asked: the flag stands are the payoff for CTF, and deathmatch modes terminate on the match timer, which is not spatial.

During the 30-second intermission, do players wait somewhere built inside the walls — a lobby or staging area — or is that just a screen between matches?

skill_gap.name: one map, several modes
skill_gap.why: the prompt asks a single arena to serve free-for-all, team deathmatch and capture the flag. Shooter's presets are one per mode and the emit block holds one shape and one preset, so a multi-mode map can only be approximated by unioning options from several presets, and nothing in the handoff records that the union was deliberate rather than a mixed-up pick.

notes_for_us: genre-choice step 5 only licenses a shape question when two shapes route differently. Here lane-network and space-bounded both route P0 but produce very different maps, so the rule as written suppresses the single most consequential question this prompt raises.

The only geometry the prompt states outright — the hollow square outer wall — has no row in Shooter's table or the universal six. It exists only as Sports' barrier-perimeter, reachable solely by loading options.md, which the skill tells you not to load by default.
Shooter's presets are one mode each, and step 3 says offer one preset. A prompt naming three modes has no sanctioned way to express that, and preset in the emit block cannot hold it.

layout-intake says emit theme null when the prompt is silent, but '3d guns without being blocky' is a visual-fidelity statement about a non-scene object. It is not theme, not layout and not really mechanics, and only lands in mechanics for want of anywhere better.
Scale: 'huge' is an extent word and layout-intake says detail wins, but nothing says whether an explicit 'huge' should push an arena off the block band it would otherwise default to.
